title: NovaMed POC scoping - quality eval plan
summary: POC scoping to align success criteria and design a quality evaluation plan for NovaMed's clinical summarization use case. Covered workload sizing, benchmark test matrix, golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination detection, format checks, scoring rubric, and timeline for a 4-week pilot and follow-up baseline benchmark. Agreed on sample sizes and next steps to share artifacts and run initial benchmarks.
next_steps: Redwood to share security docs (SOC2 + data residency notes) by 2026-11-12
Redwood SE to upload golden prompt spreadsheet and eval harness link by 2026-11-12
Customer to provide 1k de-identified clinical notes sample (schema + labels) by 2026-11-17
Schedule first benchmark run (hosted) week of 2026-11-22
action_items: Jake Miller | Send pricing + Dedicated vs Hosted comparison + security pack | due: 2026-11-12
Priya Shah | Upload golden prompts spreadsheet, eval harness repo link, and benchmark template | due: 2026-11-12
Ellie Wong | Deliver 1,000 de-identified notes + target output schema and examples | due: 2026-11-17
Dr. Samir Patel | Provide success criteria weighting (accuracy vs latency vs hallucination tolerance) | due: 2026-11-16
transcript:
[00:00] Jake Miller: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jake from Redwood, AE, and with me is Priya SE and Luis from customer success. Quick rollcall?
[00:09] Maria Lopez: Hi Maria here, product.
[00:12] Tom Chen: Tom, CTO.
[00:15] Dr. Samir Patel: Samir, head of ML.
[00:17] Ellie Wong: Ellie, data eng.
[00:20] Jake Miller: Great, goal for today is to align on POC success criteria, workload sizing, and define a quality eval plan — golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, scoring. Aim for clarity so our SE team can run the first benchmark next week. Sound good?
[00:33] Maria Lopez: Yep, that works for us. We're mostly focused on clinical summarization - turning visit notes into short structured summaries that match our output schema.
[00:40] Priya Shah: Awesome. A few clarifying q's: what does success look like for you — is it accuracy first, latency, or reducing hallucinations?
[00:48] Dr. Samir Patel: Primary is clinical correctness — hallucinations are a showstopper. We need <3% hallucination rate on key extracted fields and >95% format adherence. Latency is secondary but we want under 800ms p95 for single-note summarization for hosted, and dedicated needs to be under 300ms p95 for our live workflow.
[01:10] Tom Chen: To add, cost matters too; we can't justify a model that's 5x the cost of current baseline. We'll evaluate unit economics at 100k notes/month.
[01:20] Priya Shah: Good — those are concrete. We'll map those to measurable metrics: hallucination rate on a gold-labeled set, format adherence rate (schema fields present + types), correctness F1 for extraction fields, and latency p95.
[01:32] Jake Miller: For the POC we suggest two phases: Phase A (2 weeks) baseline + golden prompt alignment and hosted benchmarks; Phase B (2 weeks) dedicated tuning and regression runs. Runbook we'll propose: 1k de-identified notes for the gold set, 3k notes for throughput tests, and separate holdout for regression.
[01:50] Maria Lopez: 1k labeled notes is ok but will take a little time. We can provide 1k de-id in 1 week.
[01:57] Ellie Wong: We'll start prepping the export tomorrow. Format is CSV with columns: note_id, note_text, structured_labels.json (we'll share schema).
[02:05] Priya Shah: Perfect. I'll attach the exact schema. For golden prompts, we typically create ~20-30 canonical prompts per summary type (discharge summary, progress note, consult) plus some edge-case prompts. These are used for both automated scoring and human review.
[02:20] Dr. Samir Patel: How do you handle hallucination detection automatically?
[02:24] Priya Shah: Two approaches: 1) rule-based checks that verify presence/consistency of critical entities (meds, dosages, dates) against the note; 2) reference-based scoring where we compare to gold labels with fuzzy matching and flag contradictions. We also do model-agnostic consistency checks — e.g., if model asserts 'no allergies' but note lists allergy, that's a red flag.
[02:45] Jake Miller: We'll also run a hallucination classifier on outputs to surface likely hallucinations; that's part of Redwood Optimize toolkit and helps triage. Note: classifiers are tuned per POC.
[02:55] Maria Lopez: Are there typical thresholds you recommend? You mentioned <3% hallucination - is that realistic?
[03:00] Priya Shah: For clinical extraction fields that's aggressive but achievable with high-quality prompts and a curated golden set; for free-form summary text we'd expect higher. We recommend gating on structured fields first.
[03:10] Tom Chen: On benchmarks — what hardware and models are you proposing for the hosted run?
[03:15] Priya Shah: For hosted baseline we'll use open LLMs from our catalog on NVidia A100-style instances (we'll note exact variants). For Dedicated runs, we can deploy a quantized variant on T4/GPU pools or customer-provided infra if going private. There's some variability in latency; we'll record tokens/s and p95 latencies.
[03:35] Jake Miller: Example benchmark matrix: correctness F1, hallucination rate, format adherence %, latency p50/p95, throughput (notes/sec) at batch sizes, and cost per 1,000 notes. We'll produce spreadsheet columns for each.
[03:48] Dr. Samir Patel: For scoring, how do you weight these? We want a combined score but with higher weight on hallucination and correctness.
[03:55] Priya Shah: Typical rubric we propose: correctness F1 (40%), hallucination penalty (30%), format adherence (15%), latency penalty (10%), cost penalty (5%). But that's configurable — we can make a customizable scorecard and you'll choose weights.
[04:12] Maria Lopez: That makes sense. Can the grading be both automated and human-in-the-loop?
[04:16] Priya Shah: Yes. Automated scoring covers the bulk — F1, format checks, simple hallucination heuristics. We'll surface a sampled set (random + edge cases) for human review to calibrate thresholds. Human labeling rounds are usually 200-500 samples.
[04:30] Jake Miller: Let's talk about regression tests - after we iterate on prompts or model, we need a regression harness. Priya?
[04:36] Priya Shah: Regression harness will run nightly against a holdout set (500-1k notes). It will compute diff metrics vs baseline and flag any regressions beyond a delta threshold (e.g., F1 drop >2 points or hallucination increase >1%). We keep older model outputs in a small artifact store for diffs.
[04:55] Ellie Wong: How do you store outputs & logs — we need audit logs and must be compatible with our compliance team.
[04:59] Jake Miller: For hosted tests we keep audit logs and the console exposes trace IDs, per-request token counts, and redactions. For Dedicated/Private we can do customer-managed KMS and log retention policies. We'll include SOC2 details in the pack.
[05:14] Tom Chen: Any issues with PHI in the POC? We need to ensure de-id pipeline is reviewed.
[05:20] Priya Shah: Agreed — de-id before upload. We'll accept only de-identified data for hosted unless there's a contractual BA/hipaa addendum and private deployment. For the pilot we assume de-id.
[05:30] Maria Lopez: Ok. For golden prompts — can you show an example?
[05:34] Priya Shah: Sure, examples: 'Summarize the key diagnoses and discharge meds from this note in JSON with fields: diagnoses[], medications[{name, dose, route, frequency}], allergies[]'. This enforces structured output.
[05:48] Dr. Samir Patel: We need format validation to be strict — JSON schema validation and a small lenient parser for common small deviations.
[05:55] Priya Shah: We'll run a jsonschema validator. For small deviations we'll attempt auto-corrections, but those cases will be flagged in the report. Format adherence metric counts exact schema matches.
[06:06] Jake Miller: About sample sizes — we proposed 1k gold labels for correctness and hallucination checks, 3k for throughput. Is that doable?
[06:12] Maria Lopez: 1k gold will need labeling support. Could Redwood provide a labeling template so our SME can label faster?
[06:17] Priya Shah: Yes — we'll provide labeling template + example labels. We can offer up to 200 hand-labeled samples from our bench team to help initial calibration if needed.
[06:27] Tom Chen: Timeline?
[06:29] Jake Miller: Outline: Week 0 (now): agree on artifacts and schedule. Week 1: customer provides de-id samples and schema; Redwood shares golden prompts + eval harness. Week 2: Baseline hosted benchmark run and initial scores + human calibration. Week 3: Prompt tuning and regression runs. Week 4: Dedicated deployment tests (if chosen), final POC report and recommendation.
[06:51] Dr. Samir Patel: That 4-week window is reasonable. We aim to have decision by end of December.
[06:56] Maria Lopez: What about edge-case testing — rare meds or complex multi-comorbid notes?
[07:00] Priya Shah: We'll include a stratified sampling plan: easy/median/hard buckets and focused adversarial prompts. We'll also include targeted hallucination tests where we fabricate plausible but incorrect facts to test model filtering.
[07:13] Jake Miller: Let's capture acceptance thresholds again: correctness F1 > 0.86 on main extraction fields, hallucination rate < 3% on structured fields, format adherence > 95%, latency p95 < 800ms hosted baseline. Those are our starting gates; customer can tighten them.
[07:30] Dr. Samir Patel: F1 0.86 is fine as an initial threshold.
[07:33] Ellie Wong: For the benchmark run, what request patterns do you simulate?
[07:36] Priya Shah: We'll simulate mix: 80% single-note realtime flow and 20% batched backend summarization. We'll test concurrency up to the expected QPS you provided which is 8 qps sustained for user-facing flow and burst to 40 qps for backend batch jobs.
[07:53] Tom Chen: Confirming: expected monthly volume is ~100k notes, peak concurrency 40.
[07:58] Maria Lopez: Correct.
[08:00] Jake Miller: Noted. We'll size the dedicated pool recommendations after baseline. We'll also provide estimated cost per 1,000 notes across model choices.
[08:10] Priya Shah: On evaluation scoring mechanics — automated metrics: F1 for field extraction (exact + fuzzy matching), schema adherence % (jsonschema exact), hallucination score (% flagged), BLEU/ROUGE for free-form summaries but de-emphasized. Combined score computed with configurable weights; we store per-sample results so you can slice by note type.
[08:32] Maria Lopez: What about false positives in hallucination classifier? We need clarity on precision/recall tradeoffs.
[08:37] Priya Shah: We'll surface classifier confidence scores and run a small manual review to calibrate thresholds before gating. Typically we tune for high precision to avoid false alarms.
[08:47] Dr. Samir Patel: Good. Any legal/procurement asks from your side?
[08:50] Jake Miller: We'll send our standard SOW template and the security pack. For private deployments we can discuss BAAs; we'll include options.
[08:58] Maria Lopez: For reporting, can we get weekly digest and a final POC report?
[09:02] Luis Ortega: Yes — weekly status deck and final detailed report with metrics, per-sample examples, and recommended next steps.
[09:09] Tom Chen: One more question — when you do model rollbacks/regressions, how do you pin versions?
[09:13] Priya Shah: Redwood Console tracks model versions and has rollout controls (canary, A/B, automatic fallback). We keep a versioned artifact for each run and tie regression alerts to those IDs.
[09:25] Jake Miller: Ok let's recap next steps...
[09:28] Jake Miller: Action: I'll send pricing and security docs by Friday (2026-11-12). Priya will upload golden prompt spreadsheet and eval harness repo. Ellie and Samir to deliver 1k de-id notes and schema. Schedule benchmark run for week of 11/22.
[09:44] Maria Lopez: Sounds good, thanks.
[09:47] Dr. Samir Patel: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:50] Jake Miller: Thanks all. End.

Notes: Transcript has minor ASR errors (e.g., 'KV cash' vs KV cache) and some speaker overlap. Shared artifacts: security pack: https://redwood.example.com/sec-pack/NovaMed, golden prompts spreadsheet: https://redwood.example.com/poc/nova/golden-prompts.xlsx, eval harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-eval-harness (private).
